limits: Introductory chapter: no experiments beyond illustrations; the 60% figure is one 5-year period with one QDA fit and no variance or baseline accuracy given.
Authors concede lab results may drift as Python packages update.
Treats methods as usable without optimisation or theory detail (premise 3).
practices: Choose the method per application; no single approach performs best everywhere (premise 2, p7).
Understand each model's assumptions and trade-offs rather than treating methods as black boxes (p7).
Use cross-validation and the bootstrap to estimate accuracy and choose among methods (Chapter 5 summary, p11).
Linear methods often beat non-linear ones on interpretability and sometimes accuracy (p11).
Expect little predictability in market returns; strong autocorrelation would be exploitable (p3).
